about: The feature asset bundle contract. One entry per feature id; every surface reads its assets from here. Paths are repo-relative POSIX paths. A path is listed even when the file does not exist yet: this file states the target shape, and scripts/check-media-manifest.mjs reports the gap. Contract prose: docs/media-manifest.md.

conventions.renderDirNote: media/.gitignore excludes **/renders/, so canonical MP4s and clip GIFs exist only on a machine that has rendered them. A fresh clone reports them missing; that is correct, not a regression.
conventions.publishedStillDirNote: Load-bearing filenames. The Marketplace serves the last published README but resolves images against current main, so a rename or delete retroactively 404s the live listing. Overwrite in place only.

producedBy.docs/screenshots/generated/*.gif: hyperframes render in the composition dir, then the ffmpeg palettegen/paletteuse plus gifsicle encode recorded in that composition's STORYBOARD
producedBy.media/web/*: node scripts/render-web-clips.mjs, then node website/scripts/sync-media.mjs to copy into website/public/media

site.delivery: A build step copies the web outputs named here into website/public/media. Never a symlink, never a second source of truth.

readme-root.why: GitHub and vsce both resolve relative paths, and vsce rewrites them to absolute raw URLs at package time. GitHub cannot play video, so the animated surface here is a GIF.

readme-engine.why: The Spec Kit community catalog renders this file from main and cannot resolve relative paths, so every reference is an absolute raw.githubusercontent URL.

site-landing.why: Muted autoplay video with a poster is an order of magnitude lighter than a GIF, and a landing page carries several clips at once. The hero stills are crops of three of those clips, cut by scripts/build-hero-stills.mjs, because a whole IDE window shrunk into the hero column is unreadable.

site-docs.why: A guide page mostly wants one still it can point at in prose; it embeds the clip only when the point is a state change.

article.why: The blog renders from MDX on a different host. GIF and PNG travel without a build step; video would need its own copy path.

social-x.why: X crops a 1.58:1 frame badly in timeline preview. The 16:9 crop is cut once, here, instead of by the platform.

features.notes: Where inline-comments shows the comment card as an object, this runs the same surface through all four of its real states and then closes on the sidebar. The labels carry three ideas in order: catch a bad requirement while it is still a sentence, keep the note so a later session still knows what that bit was about, and show where that spec is found again. No label says the spec was rewritten, because the extension does not read the file back. The closing shot deliberately shows only Specs and Steering, the two views a fresh install with just the VS Code extension puts in the activity bar.

features.notes: Page chrome, not product imagery: the focal light a product frame sits in front of.
